text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Algeria's state-owned oil and gas Sonatrach firm to raise salaries by 15 percent for its 38,000 workers, beginning next January, the union said. Sonatrach's chairman Nazim Zouioueche worked hard to persuade the government to endorse such a hike. Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia was reluctant, arguing austerity must apply for every economic sector.
- University teachers threaten to strike next week to back claims for more pay and better working conditions.

- A draft law sets July 5, 1998 as a deadline for widespread use of the Arabic language, making its use compulsory in business and government bureaucracy. The draft law would be voted on by the Transitional National Council which began a 100-day session last Wednesday.
- Algeria's soccer team beat Ivory Coast 4-1 in their African Nations Cup qualifier match played on Sunday in Algiers.
- The authorities started a review of voter lists ahead of a referendum to amend the constitution within the next two months.
